newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end lower, crown firms.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end lower, crown firms.

text.p: 1415 GMT - Long Swedish bond yields ended lower on Friday on the back of optimism about Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), lower than expected U.S. producer prices and a firmer crown.

The crown benefited from a generally softer mark and one big buy order, dealers said. * Six-month T-bill rate flat at 4.17 pct. * Ten-year bond yield falls six basis points to 6.77 pct. * Crown firms to 4.4770 to mark vs 4.5040 late on Thursday.
Long Swedish bond yields ended lower on Friday on the back of optimism about Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), lower than expected U.S. producer prices and a firmer crown.
The crown also benefited from players expecting EMU to start on time in 1999 as well as from a generally softer mark and one big buy order, dealers said.

"Bond players were short just ahead of the U.S. PPI figure and when it turned out to have fallen by 0.3 percent instead of an expected rise of 0.1 percent, people started buying it all back," one dealer said.

The EMU optimism partly derived from Germany and France discussing the stability pact on Friday. In addition, European Union (EU) finance ministers will meet on Sunday, one day ahead of the EU summit in Amsterdam.
The six-month T-bill rate was flat at 4.17 percent while the ten-year bond yield fell six basis points to 6.77 percent.
The crown firmed to 4.4770 against the mark from 4.5040 late on Thursday.
